post.caption: Oregon sunstone's colors come from copper specks. Smaller specks make it look red, and slightly larger ones green, and one stone can hold up to three colors at once. A 1985 study found metallic copper inside the stones, and Oregon sunstone is sold as natural and untreated. Native Americans may have been the first to collect them, and the first written report came around 1908. Since 1972 the public can collect sunstones free on four square miles. Locals have called them Plush diamonds, and one rough stone from the Dust Devil mine weighed 1,093 carats. Oregon made it the state gemstone in 1987.
